title: OSHA GFCI and Grounding Checklist (29 CFR 1910.304)
subtitle: Use on a site walk-through of permanent wiring and of temporary wiring set up for construction-like work.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A.
Record each defect, keep the affected circuit, cord or equipment out of use until it is repaired, and check it again before it goes back into use.
The manufacturer's instructions and your site rules may add checks to this list.

sections.title: GFCI protection
items: Each 125-volt, single-phase, 15- or 20-ampere receptacle in a bathroom is a GFCI receptacle or is fed through GFCI protection.
Each 125-volt, single-phase, 15- or 20-ampere receptacle on the roof has GFCI protection for personnel.
Temporary 125-volt, single-phase, 15-, 20- and 30-ampere outlets in use by workers are GFCI-protected.
Each cord set used for temporary power has GFCI protection at the outlet, or a GFCI cord set or device is plugged into the receptacle closest to the power source.
Temporary receptacles of other ratings in use by personnel are GFCI-protected. If GFCI protection is not available, an assured equipment grounding conductor program is in place (Section B).
Receptacles replaced at outlets that Subpart S requires to be GFCI-protected have GFCI protection.
Grounding-type receptacles in boxes without a ground
Each one is supplied through a GFCI and marked “GFCI Protected” and “No Equipment Ground”, and no grounding conductor is connected to it.

sections.title: Assured equipment grounding conductor program (where GFCI is not available)
items: A written description of the program, with the employer's specific procedures, is on site and can be produced for inspection and copying.
At least one competent person has been named to implement the program.
Cord sets, plugs, receptacles and cord-and-plug equipment are checked before each day's use. No pins are deformed or missing, the insulation is undamaged, and there are no signs of internal damage.
Items found damaged or defective are tagged or removed and are not used until repaired.
Equipment grounding conductors have been tested for continuity and are electrically continuous.
Each receptacle and attachment cap or plug has been tested, and the grounding conductor is on its proper terminal.

Tests were done before first use, after any repair, and after any incident suspected of causing damage. The last test was no more than 3 months ago, or no more than 6 months ago for fixed items that are not exposed to damage.
Equipment that has not met the program
No equipment that has not met the program's requirements is available to employees or in use.
A log, color code or other record identifies each item that passed and shows its last test date or test interval. The record is available on site.

sections.title: Grounding and receptacle wiring
items: Ground connections from circuits, equipment and enclosures are intact and continuous, with no open grounds, removed grounding pins or broken raceway joints.
Receptacles checked show no reversed polarity, and the grounded conductor is on its designated terminal.
Receptacles on 15- and 20-ampere branch circuits are grounding type, unless they are permitted replacements.
Receptacle grounding contacts are connected to the equipment grounding conductor of the supplying circuit.
Grounding terminals on receptacles, cord connectors and plugs are used only for grounding.
Hand-held, stationary, fixed and light industrial motor-operated tools have an intact grounding conductor and grounding pin, or are covered by an exemption in 1910.304(g)(6)(vii).
Appliances in wet or damp locations
Cord-and-plug appliances used in damp or wet locations, on the ground, on metal floors, or inside metal tanks or boilers are grounded.
Metal cable trays, raceways and conductor enclosures are grounded unless an exception in 1910.304(g)(6)(i) applies.
Metal enclosures for service equipment are grounded.

sections.title: Overcurrent devices, outlets and services
items: Fuses and breakers are readily accessible to each employee or to authorized building management staff.
Overcurrent devices are not exposed to physical damage, and no easily ignitable material is nearby.
Each circuit breaker clearly shows whether it is off (open) or on (closed).
Breakers used to switch 120-volt or 277-volt fluorescent lighting are listed and marked “SWD.”
On circuits supplying two or more outlets, the cord-and-plug load on each receptacle is within the Table S-4 maximum.
On circuits supplying two or more outlets, receptacle ratings match Table S-5 for the circuit rating.
A receptacle outlet is installed wherever flexible cords with attachment plugs are used.
Where a building has more than one nominal voltage system, the phase and system identification method is permanently posted at each branch-circuit panelboard.
The service disconnect plainly shows whether it is open or closed, and it is readily accessible nearest the point where the service-entrance conductors enter.

references: 29 CFR 1910.304: Wiring design and protection (Part 1910, Subpart S: Electrical)
